No cloud credentials exist on this machine. Program rule: when live verification is blocked, build the production path, contract tests and a LIVE-TEST HARNESS, and NEVER fabricate live success. Live tests use dedicated sandbox accounts only, never an arbitrary production account; destructive actions need explicit test-environment safeguards; strong naming/tagging; cleanup workflows.

Owned paths (only these may be edited): `scripts/acceptance/**`, `tests/acceptance/**` (unit tests of the harness itself), `docs/platform/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `fixtures/acceptance-app/**`. Read-only context (do not import, they are unmerged): capability broker REST at `Z:\Projects\Spawned.ai\zenith-wt\ws-cap\src\app\api\platform\v1\**`, execution activities at `ws-act\src\lib\execution\**`, AWS drivers in `ws-aws-net/ws-aws-cmp/ws-aws-data`. Contracts are fixed (docs/platform/ARCHITECTURE.md, ADRs 0005/0006/0009/0016, deploy/aws/README.md + zenith-connection.cfn.yaml).

Deliverables:
1. `scripts/acceptance/safety.ts`: hard gates before ANY cloud call: env `ZENITH_LIVE_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` set and equal to the STS GetCallerIdentity account (ambient CLI profile only for the bootstrap check); explicit opt-in marker SSM parameter `/zenith/live-sandbox` = `true` (operator's one-time acknowledgement) else refuse; region allowlist; run id `zlive-<yyyymmddhhmm>-<rand4>` as name prefix and `zenith:live-run` tag on everything; `--confirm-billable` required for any mutating scenario (dry-run otherwise); max-cost guard (refuse when the plan estimate exceeds `ZENITH_LIVE_MAX_MONTHLY_USD`, default 50); stateful deletion only for resources carrying this run's tag.
2. `scripts/acceptance/cleanup.ts`: tag-based sweeper (Resource Groups Tagging API, `zenith:live-run=<id>`, or all `zlive-*` older than N hours with `--older-than`), deletes via `tofu destroy` of the run workspace when state exists, else native deletes in dependency order (ECS services -> ALB -> target groups -> RDS (skip final snapshot ONLY for run-tagged) -> ElastiCache -> subnets/SG -> VPC; S3 empty+delete; SQS; log groups; ECR force); each deletion re-checks the tag right before deleting; dry-run by default; JSON report.
3. `scripts/acceptance/evidence.ts`: recorder writing under the OS temp dir by default (`--out` overrides; .gitignore is NOT yours): step timings, operation ids, plan digests, http probes, log query results (redacted via `redactCredentials`), final summary stating exactly which checks ran live and which were skipped; never marks a skipped check as passed.
4. `scripts/acceptance/scenarios/*.ts`: catalogue of Demos A-J as executable definitions (id, title, prerequisites, steps, pass criteria, proves, cannot prove): A autonomous AWS deploy (repo -> analysis -> proposal -> plan -> approval -> deploy -> DNS/TLS -> health); B incident diagnosis (break DB SG rule, sandbox-only, run-tagged); C approved remediation; D drift (external modification + detection); E restart recovery (kill execution worker mid-apply -> `uncertain` or durable completion, never unsafe replay); F credential revocation (revoke agent/runner access -> next request fails); G Kubernetes deploy (kind or sandbox cluster); H MCP (connect a coding agent, inspect, propose, approve, execute); I managed provider (provider=zenith); J multi-cloud planning (plan only; MUST run end to end locally now using merged placement + resources). Scenarios that depend on unmerged modules call small interfaces (`ControlPlaneClient` over REST `/api/platform/v1` + workflow client) with fetch-based implementations; runnable later with configuration only. Each scenario has `--dry-run` printing the exact planned actions and checking prerequisites with no cloud call.
5. `scripts/acceptance/aws-live.ts`: CLI `npx tsx scripts/acceptance/aws-live.ts --scenario A --confirm-billable` wiring safety -> scenario -> evidence -> cleanup (cleanup ALWAYS attempted in `finally`, cleanup failures reported loudly).
6. `fixtures/acceptance-app/`: tiny dependency-free Node HTTP app, `/health`, `/db` as a TCP connect check to host:port parsed from `DATABASE_URL`, Dockerfile (node:22-alpine pinned by digest, non-root), README.
7. `docs/platform/ACCEPTANCE.md`: how to run each scenario, required sandbox setup (the CloudFormation stack from deploy/aws, the SSM marker, budget-alarm recommendation), expected costs, cleanup, and a status table (no scenario has run live; J runs locally; which are blocked on what).

Required tests (`tests/acceptance/**`, Vitest, `*.test.ts`, node env): safety gates refuse wrong account / missing marker / missing confirm flag / over-budget plan / non-run-tagged deletion (use `aws-sdk-client-mock`); cleanup ordering + tag re-check + dry-run default; evidence recorder never marks skipped as passed and redacts canaries; catalogue completeness (A-J present, each with pass criteria and "cannot prove" text); Demo J runs end to end locally and its output includes cross-cloud egress/latency lines; the sample app's /db check times out against a closed/non-routable port.

## 4. Remaining (do in this order)

1. `scenarios/e-restart-recovery.ts` (`demoE`, dependsOn A). Design: (a) check `createWorkerController(config.workerControl)` and Temporal availability (`ctx.workflows.available()`); (b) change the manifest (`buildLiveManifest({replicas: 2, ...})` + `project.updateManifest` via `runAction`) so a second deploy has a long apply; (c) propose `deployment.deploy`, `awaitApproval`; (d) poll `ctx.workflows.getProgress(opId)` until an `apply_*` step is `running` (the query needs a live worker); (e) `ctx.worker.kill()` (SIGKILL); (f) with the worker down, `ctx.workflows.describe(opId)` must say RUNNING (durable) and the control-plane operation must not flip to failed; (g) `ctx.worker.start()`, wait for terminal. Criteria: `crash-injected` (kill done while the step was running), `durable` (workflow RUNNING while the worker was down), `terminal-safe` (final status `succeeded` or `uncertain`, NEVER `failed` after a replay), `no-unsafe-replay` (operation events show a single `operation.started`; after recovery exactly one ECS service per manifest service exists in the run's tag listing; if `uncertain`, no new apply event follows). `blockedOn`: real activities with lease + fence handling (WS-ACT), a worker under harness control (`ZENITH_LIVE_WORKER_CONTROL`), Temporal.

10. `docs/platform/ACCEPTANCE.md`: how to run each scenario (commands; `--dry-run` first), sandbox setup (deploy the `deploy/aws` CloudFormation stack, optionally with `NameSuffix`; the SSM marker `aws ssm put-parameter --name /zenith/live-sandbox --type String --value true` created by the account OWNER with their own profile — Zenith's observe role is explicitly denied `ssm:GetParameter*`, so the marker can only be read with the operator's ambient profile; a Route53 zone and `Route53HostedZoneArns`; a verified connection id; an AWS Budgets alarm recommendation, e.g. $25/month with email + SNS), the env var table (from `config.ts`), expected costs (the local estimate for the sample app is likely well above the default $50/month guard because of NAT + ALB + RDS; a run lasts about an hour so real spend is cents, but the guard measures the MONTHLY rate, so raise `ZENITH_LIVE_MAX_MONTHLY_USD` deliberately, e.g. 150; compute the real number with `buildLiveManifest({runId:"zlive-202609301200-ab12", region:"us-east-1"}).estimateUsd` and put it in the doc), cleanup (dry run first, `--execute`, `--older-than`, what is reported, tagging-index lag, the state bucket is retained), the human approval step (the harness cannot approve), and a STATUS TABLE: live runs: NONE yet (say so plainly); local: J only; blocked: A-I with the concrete reasons from each scenario's `blockedOn`.
11. Run J for real and capture its evidence summary: `npx tsx scripts/acceptance/aws-live.ts --scenario J` (after step 7); paste `summary.md` into the final handoff.
12. Final checks: `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole repo, ~60 s, must be clean), `npx eslint scripts/acceptance tests/acceptance fixtures/acceptance-app`, `npx vitest run tests/acceptance`; commit on `ws/live` (a normal commit message, no `wip:`), then write the final handoff per WORKER-BRIEF.md.

## 6. Decisions and assumptions already made (do not undo)

- The harness never approves anything: `POST /api/platform/v1/operations/:id/approve` is browser-session-only (it refuses any Authorization header). Scenarios wait for a human. If policy allows unattended execution (the sandbox default autonomy 4 allows `deployment.deploy`), the approval criterion is recorded SKIPPED, not passed. `ControlPlaneClient` has no approve method.
- The harness uses the operator's AMBIENT sandbox credentials only for: bootstrap identity/marker checks, verification reads, out-of-band changes that stand in for the outside world (Demos B and D), tag adoption and cleanup. Zenith's own actions always go through the control plane and broker. The SSM marker is read with the ambient profile because `ZenithObservePolicy` denies `ssm:GetParameter*`.
- CONTRACT GAP found and worked around: the execution worker's `baseTags` (ws-act `src/lib/execution/session.ts`) applies `zenith:managed`, `zenith:workspace`, `zenith:project`, `zenith:environment` but NO per-run tag, and names resources `zenith-<environmentId>` (a product-generated id), not `zenith-<runId>`. So the harness creates one dedicated Zenith environment per run (`env.create` with `name = runId`), records its id in `<evidence dir>/run-state.json` immediately, and ADOPTS (`adopt.ts`, tagging API `TagResources`) everything whose `zenith:environment` tag equals that id and that has no other run's tag. The cleanup name guard accepts a name containing the runId OR a recorded environment id. Requested changes: WS-ACT should let `baseTags` merge an allowlisted extra-tags setting (at least `zenith:live-run`); WS-TOFU should add `destroy` to `TofuRun` (the harness has its own destroy runner in `tofu-destroy.ts`).
- `tofu destroy` path: an empty workspace assembled with the pinned provider set and the s3 backend key `zenith/<workspace>/<environment>/terraform.tfstate` in `zenith-state-<account>-<region>`; the destroy PLAN is verified tag by tag before apply (everything is refused if any resource is not provably the run's). Refresh must stay on (the default) so out-of-band adopted tags are visible.
- The product's `/api/health/:envId` is ALWAYS simulated and `/api/environments/:id/drift` can be simulated. A `simulated: true` response is never live evidence (Demo D fails its criteria rather than passing).
- Run id format `zlive-<yyyymmddhhmm UTC>-<4 chars [a-z0-9]>`; the age for `--older-than` is parsed from the id (the tagging API has no creation time). Tags: `zenith:managed=true`, `zenith:environment=<runId>`, `zenith:live-run=<runId>`.
- The region has NO default (`ZENITH_LIVE_REGION` or `--region`; it must be in `ZENITH_LIVE_ALLOWED_REGIONS`, default `us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-south-1`). Default budget guard is 50 USD/month; an unknown estimate is refused.
- Dry run = no cloud call at all; only offline prerequisites are evaluated unless `--check-control-plane`. Cleanup is dry-run by default (`--execute` deletes). Cleanup lists the run region plus us-east-1 (global services).
- `unsupported` resource types are reported loudly and left alone; cleanup `ok` is false for any failed/refused/unsupported/remaining.
- The evidence verdict rules (section 3) and "a criterion no step recorded is SKIPPED" are deliberate honesty guarantees; keep them.
- Scenario criteria are `{id,text}` objects; steps record results with the `checker(...)` helpers; `dependsOn` means "must have completed earlier in the same `--scenario A,B,C` run" (state shared via `ctx.state`; no adopting of old runs).
- Sample app: dependency-free; `/health` never touches the DB (so Demo B's outage must be diagnosed, not fixed by a restart); `/db` is a TCP connect check only (proves the security-group/network path, not auth or Postgres health); credentials from DATABASE_URL are never echoed.
- Child processes (tofu via the merged `buildChildEnv`/`runProcess`, docker via `worker-control.ts`) get explicit allowlisted environments.
- No dependency changes were needed. SDK clients used: sts, ssm, resource-groups-tagging-api, ecs, ec2, elastic-load-balancing-v2, rds, elasticache, s3, sqs, cloudwatch-logs, cloudwatch, ecr, secrets-manager, acm, iam, lambda, route-53.
- I ran `docker pull node:22-alpine` once to read the digest (public image); nothing else was downloaded.
